data.name: Master Spy
data.detailed_description:
Throw on your invisibility cloak and put your reflexes to the test in this brutal precision platformer brimming with espionage, intrigue, and betrayal!

You are Master Spy.


In a world of corruption and decay, you're not just good at what you do - you're the best. And with the aid of your prototype cloaking suit and quick wit, you'll sneak your way past a multitude of enemies and obstacles, all while uncovering a plot of conspiracy and intrigue that thrusts you into a role far greater than your contract promised.

Confidential Details:

  • Jump, sneak, and cloak your way through more than 50 challenging levels, with locales ranging from churning electro factories to mystical ninja command centers!
  • Cinematic pixel art cutscenes pull you into the experience, weaving a tale of espionage, intrigue, and betrayal!
  • Discover Secret levels hidden throughout the game, allowing you to change the story!
  • Put your skills to the ultimate test in the unlockable limited-visibility Blind Master mode!
  • Train in the *new* Novice mode with checkpoints that aid you on your mission!
  • Play in Narrative Mode at your own pace - enjoy the cutscenes and OST without getting caught!
  • Stuck? Switch between Narrative, Novice, and Operative modes right from the pause menu!
  • Jam in that cheat code to play any level and watch the cutscenes at your leisure!

Featuring an Original Soundtrack by Grammy Award Winner André Allen Anjos / RAC.

reviews.review:
6,5/10
A die&retry mixed with stealth elements, which shines more through its art than through its gameplay. 
Master Spy is a very precise platformer, but the precision required is not as pixel perfect as in a game like Super Meat Boy. The difficulty is mainly due to many sequences of synchronized actions. Towards the ends, it requires coordination and reaction time in the order of 0.1 second.
There are only two actions, jumping and becoming invisible. While invisible, moving is considerably slowed down. While visible, being spotted by the humans and robots is as instantly fatal as the various traps found throughout the game.
There is also a "double jump". It doesn't make the jump higher but longer. And executing it requires a good timing.
For the first half of the game, each level consist of 1 or 2 screens with 1 or 2 key cards to collect to unlock the door that lead to the next level.
Later it can consist of bigger levels with multiple checkpoint. And thankfully there are checkpoints, because the game is very hard!

Positive points
The pixel art is good and varied with many little details. Scenery is renewed at each stage with each time new traps and ennemies.
Excellent soundtrack. My favorite song is the final mission/menu theme.
There is a simple story about a reel containing secret infos, and Master Spy is sent to retrieve it. It's told through cutscene in an 80' anime style between each five missions. While I didn't think much of it at the beginning, I was quite hooked towards the end. Objectively, the cutscene aren't much animated but I still found them extremely stylish. I would be very interested in watching an anime where I could follow the adventure of this most professional spy in the world.
The game has four different difficulties, "Narrative" < "Novice" < "Operative" < "Master". For reference I've chosen 'Operative', and while very hard for me, it was quite doable until the end because of the checkpoints. If you can't manage a level, it's still possible to change the difficulty whenever you want.
Once the game finished, there are two new things. First a new "Blind" mode, but it's reserved for the masochists that enjoy their tendency in the most extreme way. Because in this mode, every level are played in the dark with only the zone close to Master Spy remaining visible. Secondly, it's now possible to find an alternative ending which was worth it in my opinion. To obtain it, the entire game must be replayed while finding and beating every "VR" levels hidden inside the existing levels. Forum research advised, or else they are near impossible to find.

Negative points
The gameplay is a bit rigid and it's the main problem of this game. First, the animation is a bit too stiff, for both enemies and Master Spy. Secondly, the jump height is fixed, it's impossible to perform a small jump. And finally, I find the hitbox a bit too big.
There is also no possibility of reconfiguring the controls, no achievement and no steam cloud.

The game delivers a grade at the end of each mission, and it clearly displayed my shameful skills, "F" most of the time. And at the end of the game: 1659 captures/death! ^^
